problem.name: Welded-tree traversal
problem.statement_latex:
Two depth-$h$ binary trees have their leaves joined by a random alternating cycle; vertex names are random strings. Given the entrance root and an oracle returning neighbors, output the other root. The graph has $N=\Theta(2^h)$ vertices and constant degree. This is a graph-search oracle problem exhibiting structural exponential advantage.
Complexity counts neighbor-oracle queries and quantum gates in the random-label oracle model.
problem.statement_text: Two depth-$h$ binary trees have their leaves joined by a random alternating cycle; vertex names are random strings. Given the entrance root and an oracle returning neighbors, output the other root. The graph has $N=\Theta(2^h)$ vertices and constant degree. This is a graph-search oracle problem exhibiting structural exponential advantage. Complexity counts neighbor-oracle queries and quantum gates in the random-label oracle model.

quantum.headline_latex: $\operatorname{poly}(h)$ queries and gates, the Childs et al. continuous-time quantum walk.
quantum.details_latex: The graph has $\Theta(2^h)$ vertices, but its column symmetry confines the relevant evolution to a polynomial-dimensional effective path. The oracle implements sparse-graph evolution from the entrance, and measurement finds the exit with probability amplified to a constant.

classical.headline_latex: $2^{\Omega(h)}$ queries in the worst case, classical randomized oracle exploration.
classical.details_latex: The original lower bound shows that an algorithm making at most $2^{h/6}$ queries has exponentially small success probability. Breadth-first exploration gives an $O(2^h)$ upper bound. Random labels and the hidden leaf welding prevent a classical query algorithm from reconstructing the useful column structure with polynomially many queries.

hardware.description_latex: Fault-tolerant digital simulation uses $O(h)$ vertex-label qubits plus sparse-Hamiltonian simulation and oracle workspace. A physical analog realization with one site per graph vertex instead needs $\Theta(2^h)$ sites, a distinct resource model.
